title: phase-u: Strict managed lint adoption, compatible wheels and CLI reference
description:
## Goal
Deliver strict managed sc-lint 0.8.5, approved dependency/refactor carry-in, #648 CLI-reference delivery and #820 stable-ABI wheels for release 1.8.0. This incorporates the user-approved decisions after the exact dfa1d89c plan approval; the requested narrow quality-mgr glance applies to this decision update. No new review machinery or product capability is claimed by these plan edits.

## Sprint set / agent level
| Sprint | Scope | Hard prerequisites | Agent level |
|---|---|---|---|
| U.1 | Recovered carry-in / MiniJinja 2.18.x correction | selected base / authorized handoff | fast |
| U.2 | Approved strict policy input | U.1 | normal |
| U.3 | ONE existing-refactor verification batch: CLI / Beads / Composer | U.1 | normal |
| U.4 | Final ABI-aware cross contract | U.2 | frontier |
| U.5 | Managed 0.8.5 kit, adapter and root tooling | U.4 | frontier |
| U.6 | Clap reference generator and website | U.1 | normal |
| U.7 | ABI3 features, Python floor audit, limited API | U.1 | frontier |
| U.8 | Workflow wheels, compatibility procedure, small CI, local rehearsal | U.7 | normal |
| U.9 | Shared delivery wiring and complete phase acceptance | U.3, U.5, U.6, U.8 | frontier |
Agent levels are dispatch requirements, not named people or fixed model IDs. Metadata agent_level is fast/normal/frontier; installed-schema difficulty maps frontier to hard, normal to normal and fast to fast. Do not read layer numbers as serial dependencies.

## User-approved decisions — D1-D7 CLOSED (2026-11-03)
D1 APPROVED: [line_counts] max_production_lines=1000, no exclusions.
D2 APPROVED: exact identity policy and canonical env owners from the reviewed proposal; ONE canonical non-Rust JSON fixture supplies policy/test token data, including ATM_HOME; repo_boundaries.rs removes concat! and loads the fixture. Forbidden literals remain randlee/team-lead/arch-comp/arch-ccomp/comp/comps/team-lead@example.invalid/ATM_HOME; canonical owners remain template_store.rs for SC_COMPOSE_DATA_DIR/SC_COMPOSE_TEMPLATE_DIR and commands/template_lint.rs for SC_COMPOSE_TEMPLATE_CONTRACTS_SCOPE.
D3 APPROVED — FIX #787, owner comp's recovery replay, recorded by U.1: wheel compose(), compose_file() and render_loaded_template() always apply the CLI checked-render contract to JSON outputs selected by extension/format, raising ScRenderError ERR_RENDER_JSON_MALFORMED. Replay source 588ab3d7 / prior replay 49e4dd59, with a caller-visible CHANGELOG Fixed entry naming #787. Drop a50d4d9f/e8143961 opt-in variants. Preserve non-JSON bytes and schema-less MiniJinja rendering semantics; D7 explicitly exempts only the approved malformed-JSON checked-output behavior, not unrelated legacy behavior.
D4 APPROVED: CPython >=3.9 floor. D5 APPROVED: ALL THREE Python distributions use abi3: sc-compose, sc-sha, sc-composer-beads (bindings/python, bindings/sc-sha-python, bindings/sc-composer-beads-python).
D6 APPROVED: Route B, selected base rebuild/from-main@6f44886d4726f3730bec3b4e343ced977f245a9a, parent f4f11cf8261770e759a6b168890233b039b9551b. Actual integration reset and later develop replacement follow L1-L4; this planning task performs neither.
D7 APPROVED: v1.7.0 Rust/Python/CLI/overlaid-suite/schema-less compatibility gate in U.9, with the sole caller-visible #787 JSON bug-fix exception in D3. Closed decisions are not claims their implementation has landed or passed.

## 1.8.0 issue ledger
| Issue | Owner / outcome |
|---|---|
| #648 | U.6 generator/site, U.9 actual offline installer/release/check wiring; required |
| #817 | Existing #839 carry-in in U.1, verified in final graph by U.9; no waiver/parser redesign |
| #820 | U.7 ABI and U.8 real wheel installs, U.9 small CI / installer inputs, with procedure evidence and findings; required |
| #819 | Superseded; close when #820 lands, no separate per-cp314 project |
Use planned/1.8.0 during planning; released/1.8.0 only at actual publication after Phase U. No publish/release sprint or issue mutation in this local edit.

## Wheel failures: observed vs coverage
- Build cause: the existing release build action defaults to CPython 3.11 and the bindings do not enable abi3, yielding cp311-cp311 wheels. That fixed-version ABI is why a 3.14 binary-wheel resolver cannot use them. Enabling abi3 is the fix; building six separate version-specific wheels is not required. A fixed build interpreter remains valid when the emitted ABI floor/tag is correct.
- #611 reports a concrete pip download sc-compose==1.6.1 --python-version 3.14 --only-binary=:all: resolution failure; published artifacts were cp311-cp311, not abi3: https://github.com/randlee/sc-compose/issues/611 .
- #611 reports a locally built 1.7.0 extension failing import on one macOS 27 / arm64 / Homebrew Python 3.14.7 setup; the later correction explicitly leaves linker/loader root cause unconfirmed: https://github.com/randlee/sc-compose/issues/611#issuecomment-6344556681 . Published cp311 wheel import was reported working in Python 3.11.13.
- #820 reports installer rejection/PATH-dependent selection when host Python differs from the existing 3.11 requirement, motivating a >=3.9 wheel contract: https://github.com/randlee/sc-compose/issues/820 .
The 4 platforms x CPython 3.9-3.14 = 24 cells, each pip+uv, are a user-approved compatibility PROCEDURE covering all three packages per cell, NOT 24 reproduced failures or a mandatory preflight/publish gate. This plan edit did not rerun those historical reproductions. Intel macOS/Windows ARM wheel gaps in #611 remain triage candidates, not added release targets.

## Ledger candidates — user triage pending, NOT committed sprints
One read of gh issue list --state open supplied the following candidates. Titles are evidence of reported defects, not fresh reproduction or an approved fix commitment.
| Issue | Reported defect / triage question |
|---|---|
| #169 | Quadratic rejection latency for deeply nested var-file input |
| #601 | release-preflight package-check-plan generator crash silently passes |
| #615 | Bead render rejects missing .beads/formulas directory |
| #818 | frontmatter-init relative --file fails with empty canonicalized root |
| #611 | Wheel compatibility/platform coverage; overlap with #820, with macOS Intel/Windows ARM requests outside #820's current four-platform matrix |
| #505 | Release notes template not consumed by automation |
| #502 | Release-note included-packages table missing sc-sha and Scoop |
| #357 | temp_root non-RAII leaks reported across test files |
| #240 | Config parse diagnostics lack path/line/column attribution |
| #361 | Old sc-lint boundary helper cargo-runs absent consumer package; triage whether U.5 resolves it, not a new sprint |
These remain candidates until user triage; no auto-close, label change or scope admission. #613/#614 are already labeled shipped/1.7.0 in the issue listing and are not newly scheduled defects. #503 is an ATM ownership report, not admitted to this standalone toolchain.

## Follow-on only
Held toml1, quick-xml0.42, MiniJinja3, clap/serde/thiserror and duplicate-version upgrades remain out of scope. No 1.7.1 changelog/metadata wholesale replay or advisory/identity/size/Clippy exception.
design:
## Boundary map
- BOUNDARY-ScCompose owns sc-lint process invocation/normalization/report HTML and root developer orchestration; sc-lint owns rules and envelopes. Preserve fixed executable/allowlisted descriptors (ADR0016/0017).
- BOUNDARY-ScComposer stays pure: private completed composition/extraction/schema changes preserve API/diagnostic/span semantics; no CLI/ATM dependencies.
- BOUNDARY-ScComposerBeads retains host-neutral argv/receipts/graph/quoting; no test-support dependency reintroduction (ADR0021/0023).
- Directed edges stay CLI->composer/beads, beads->composer, composer->sc-sha, Python/Go adapters->owned libraries. Inventory corrections#836, Zlib removal#837, dev-edge removal#838, YAML advisory repair#839, generator repair#840 and stale workspace cleanup#841 are finished inputs, not new scope.

## Landing rules — sole owner (L1-L4)
L1. The user selected rebuild/from-main@6f44886d4726f3730bec3b4e343ced977f245a9a (parent f4f11cf8) as the Phase U base: Route B overlay and receiver-contract alignment are done, #787 replay is comp's remaining approved recovery work, and integrate/phase-u is to be reset to the selected SHA only after the pending user go-ahead. Record that base plus any subsequent approved #787 replay head/mapping; never substitute caa43cfc/acf55fba or import quarantined strict-only ancestry. The observed base is lint-RED on sc-lint 0.8.4 (version, pytests, function-length, line-counts, identity-literals, check.xwin, clippy.xwin); these are Phase U closure work, not an existing green claim. U.1 additionally constrains MiniJinja spec+lock to 2.18.x with bool/schema-less regression because the base and #823+ otherwise float to 2.24.0; MiniJinja 3 remains held. This planner does not reset any ref.
L2. After the authorized base handoff and classification of the known CI state, comp lands the frozen #831 plus 17 #825 carry-in rows EARLY on integrate/phase-u, #831 first, without waiting for U.9. Preserve original QA/source mappings and accepted adaptations/drop dispositions in U.1's sole table; earlier 0.4.0 setup exit3 is historical contract evidence, not the complete current-base diagnosis.
L3. One authorized stack writer acts at a time; isolated developers deliver disjoint paths. Layer numbers/PR lower bounds do not impose serial development. Comp lands the approved 25 refactor deltas plus #842 after U.1 before U.3 verifies that exact candidate; unresolved verification findings route to corrective layers and block U.9, never become fixed-by-U.3 claims. Original frozen provenance is retained and changes are explicitly mapped/rechecked.
L4. After exact-head U.9 aggregate/whole-phase review and explicit user approval, develop is REPLACED by integrate/phase-u through the approved guarded recovery procedure with a review-only PR, not merged: merging cannot remove 8b6294f1 from develop ancestry. The authorized lead/writer freezes exact source/target heads, verifies backups/explicit lease and approved tree identity, and stops on lease/protection failure; affected checks rerun on changes. This is a future user-approved destructive handoff, not authorization for this planner to execute it. No direct sprint PR lands develop. Publication follows Phase U.

## Parallel execution and file ownership
After U.1, dispatch U.2/U.3/U.6/U.7 concurrently; all decisions are approved, while base handoff/reset still needs the explicit L1 action authorization. U.3 is read-only over a fixed candidate, with three crate sections in one batch. U.2->U.4->U.5 owns root policy/cross/managed files; U.4 uses approved D4/D5 without waiting for U.7 implementation; U.9 executes the declared rows against that ABI code. U.6 owns only generator/CLI docs/site files and uses existing dependencies, not Cargo.lock. U.7 owns binding sources/manifests and Cargo.lock, no root lint/CI files. U.8 follows U.7 ABI code and owns the dispatch-only wheel procedure/workflow and its normal evidence; U.9 wires only the small artifact-consuming CI test, never a matrix preflight or publish gate. U.9 consumes the producer contracts to wire shared Justfile/CI/installer inputs once; U.5 also installs the supported sc-publish /prerelease kit. No matrix-to-preflight or publish-assignment verification interface exists. This is why U.6 and U.7 have no dependency on one another or U.5.
Planned critical path 5 (U.1->U.2->U.4->U.5->U.9); width 4; 9 sprints. The previous graph had critical path 8 and 11 sprints; this is a dependency count, not a claim about elapsed implementation time. Shared paths always have a real dependency path, not a fabricated serial edge between unrelated features. No U.6->U.7 documentation-to-ABI edge or required throwaway 0.8.4 cross success.

## Evidence lifetime — sole owner (E1-E3)
E1. U.1's one table serves the authorized carry-in writer and U.9 reviewer, gating preservation/accounting of the real 18-PR recovery input. Stop maintaining it after carry-in acceptance except for an actual changed-head disposition; archive as normal phase history at closure. Before import this payload/index/DAG are the local plan; after import the payload is historical import evidence and Beads is authoritative. Regenerate required DAG from that authority, never maintain another decision ledger or certificate.
E2. Tests/builds/checkers emit normal stdout/stderr, exit/results, candidate SHA, CI run/artifact links and necessary wheel hashes. U.3/U.5/U.8/U.9 consume them for actual size/lint/install/legacy-behavior findings. The 24-cell wheel procedure writes per-cell step.json plus one aggregate as normal evidence, with no new shared schema, mandatory preflight gate or publish-assignment verification step; failures are findings, never fabricated successes or automatic #820 closure. Reuse same-head evidence; changed code/configuration or failures justify reruns. Required results and wheel artifacts must remain accessible through the independent acceptance/review that consumes them; an expired/missing run or artifact is not PASS evidence. If existing retention expires first, retain the needed artifact through existing CI controls or rerun the affected exact-candidate build/checks and use the new actual hashes, never reconstruct a certificate. Use existing CI artifact-retention policy; after final acceptance stop actively maintaining verification summaries and let scratch/log artifacts expire normally. No new evidence service, manual matrix database, duplicate proof certificate or committed reports/**. Persistent regression tests and shipped docs are product assets, not temporary evidence.
E3. Remove disposable local-index services/environments, baseline-suite overlays and temporary build/install worktrees after results are captured, on success or failure. Keep only ordinary CI results/hash links needed for the actual acceptance; no baseline fork or ongoing rehearsal infrastructure. The private rehearsal never uploads to PyPI/TestPyPI.

## Release and technical contract
0.8.5 is an explicit release gate, not assumed published. Confirm kit/native/wheel versions, helper policy/default profile/logging/artifacts support, corrected managed Python PATH, ARM64 support and packaged pytests fix from the actual released artifact before U.5/U.9. Retain packaged pytests; do not omit it to pass0.8.4. The sc-lint lead confirmed work lint-085.18/QA lint-085.19; research handoffs are in /Users/randlee/.codex/reports/sc-lint-0.8.4-adoption-plan-20261103/upstream-confirmed-reply*.txt.
Analyzer exit10 keeps ok:true/data.findings; helper exit5 has ok:false/error.details.findings, capped10 plus true findings_count. Preserve raw exit/envelope and true totals. Config errors3/usage2/profile.steps_failed failed_steps[{index,name,exit_code,message,step_log_destination?,step_log_error?}]. Version uses data.version+self_contained. Never let the consumer reporter's legacy Findings exit0 make a strict gate green.

## Sanity / scope
Read-only dev-sanity verifies numbered deliverables from existing evidence, without rerunning lint or duplicating QA. D1-D7 are explicitly user-approved with the named implementation owners; pending implementation is not a reopened policy decision. Flaky tests are redesigned with controlled inputs, not sleeps/races/load. The user now authorizes review/fix iterations until no issues remain, followed by independent quality-mgr review. This does not create permanent review machinery. The exact dfa1d89c plan PASS is recorded; this decision update requires only the requested narrow exact-SHA quality-mgr glance, not a new broad round.
acceptance_criteria:
1. U.9's single authoritative aggregate checklist passes for the full exact candidate; all carried/new code, #648/#817/#820 and superseded #819 are accounted for. Unimplemented records remain open.
2. Apply root landing rules L1-L4 and evidence rules E1-E3. No duplicate landing policy on stack/sprints; U.1 has the only source-head checklist. D1-D7 user approvals remain explicit; pending reset/replay/implementation is tracked separately.
3. Sprint index/DAG represent only actual hard prerequisites with disjoint concurrent write ownership. All sprints specify agent_level fast/normal/frontier; metadata difficulty maps frontier to installed hard without inventing model IDs.
4. This revision stays local: strict render, validate-plan, DAG regeneration and local commit only. No import/pour/push/PR/stack mutation/publish. After local review/fix convergence submit the exact final commit to quality-mgr; only that reviewer can grant new approval. Plan validation is not product execution evidence.

title: u-3: refactor-verification-batch
description:

Do not test or ordinary-merge the contaminated source branch as the recovered candidate. Verification starts only when that concrete head is available. No recreation, splitting of the frozen branch, fresh commit quota or separate dev/sanity cycle for each section.

title: u-8: wheel-install-validation
description:
## Approved wheel procedure and small sprint CI — not a publish gate
All three distributions use abi3 with a 3.9 floor. The 24 interpreter/platform cells are an evidence procedure, not a preflight gate, publish-assignment verify step or shared-schema project.
## Deliverables
1. Provide .github/workflows/wheel-compat.yml with workflow_dispatch as its ONLY trigger: no push, pull_request or workflow_call trigger. Build each required platform/package wheel once in a workflow and identify every artifact by sha256. The full procedure consumes those workflow-built wheels, never local source builds. Test all three packages in each of 24 cells (CPython 3.9-3.14 x macOS arm64/manylinux aarch64/manylinux x86_64/Windows amd64), pip and uv. Use macOS arm64 on the host and Linux aarch64 in Colima with downloaded workflow artifacts; Windows amd64 and manylinux x86_64 run on GitHub in the manually dispatched workflow because there is no Windows amd64 hardware.
2. Emit one step.json per cell plus one aggregate evidence summary of actual commands, interpreter/platform, wheel hashes, package/import outcomes and failures. No new shared schema or mandatory result validator. Failed cells become ordinary findings; never turn failure into PASS, automatically close #820, or bolt on a mandatory publication/preflight gate.
3. Keep sprint CI small: one Linux sc-compose abi3 wheel is built ONCE by the manual builder, cached by all relevant binding/linked-library source inputs, Cargo.lock and PyO3/maturin versions, and passed as an artifact to exactly two install cells (3.9 floor and one current version, initially 3.14), pip plus uv. Push/PR jobs only consume the keyed artifact: they never rebuild a wheel or run the 24-cell procedure. A missing/stale artifact is reported accurately with the manual-build action needed; it is not a fabricated install PASS or an implicit source-build fallback.
4. Retain the disposable local-index rehearsal on the same workflow wheel hashes, with no registry uploads or publishing. Demonstrate missing-wheel, incompatible-tag/floor and source-fallback outcomes as findings/evidence, not a new release gate. Hand U.9 the small-CI artifact-consumption entry and the procedure/evidence locations; no staged-wheel preflight checker or publish-assignment verification contract.
design:
Agent level: normal. U.7 supplies the approved ABI3 package sources; the manual workflow produces the actual wheels. One 24-cell procedure covers all three packages within each cell (72 package/cell observations, each pip+uv), not 72 workflow jobs or 24 known failures. Each package/platform wheel hash is reused across that platform's six interpreter cells. Install into clean environments outside checkout without cargo/rustc on the consumer PATH; assert installed version/module location and forbid cached preinstalled/editable/source substitutions. A fixed build interpreter is valid with correct abi3 tags; six separate version-specific builds do not satisfy the intent.
Venues are fixed by the user: macOS arm64 host, Colima Linux aarch64, GitHub Windows amd64 and manylinux x86_64 (workflow_dispatch only). No Windows hardware is assumed. Record host/SDK versions; a different OS/SDK does not reproduce the separately reported unconfirmed macOS linker/loader symptom. The normal small-CI consumer takes only a source/tool-version-keyed workflow artifact and executes 3.9 plus 3.14 installs; all actual build work is in the manual builder, not push/PR jobs. Cache key covers linked Rust sources as well as binding sources so source changes cannot reuse an unrelated wheel.
Per-cell step.json and the aggregate are local procedure evidence, not an atm-core/shared contract, no schema package and no preflight/publish verification interface. Use ordinary CI/files under E2/E3; cleanup local index/environments afterward. sc-publish remains at zero new mandatory gates. Wheel prerelease support is unconfirmed; this procedure downloads normal workflow artifacts independently of CLI /prerelease archives.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Controlled checks prove workflow_dispatch is the sole full-procedure trigger; push/PR CI never builds a wheel or starts the 24-cell matrix. The small path consumes one matching cached Linux sc-compose abi3 artifact and executes only two Python-version install cells, each pip+uv, with no stale/source fallback or false PASS on a missing artifact.
2. Execute/document the 24-cell procedure over all three packages using the approved venues and workflow-built sha256 artifacts. Per-cell step.json and aggregate evidence accurately include failures, which are filed as findings. This procedure is NOT a mandatory preflight/publish/assignment-verify gate and all-cells-green is not silently reintroduced as one.
3. Local-index rehearsal and deterministic negative demonstrations use those same artifacts, no registry uploads or publishing. cargo test --workspace and focused procedure/artifact-selection fixtures run; fixture tests do not pretend the native installs happened.
4. U.9 receives real procedure outcomes/findings plus the small-CI consumer contract. Do not automatically close #820 with failed/unrun cells; account for the real state in the existing ledger. No common step.json schema or staged-wheel rejection service is created.
